currentCard.prompt: Два образца воздуха имеют одинаковую температуру. У первого точка росы 16 °C, у второго — 8 °C. В каком образце больше водяного пара?

answers.note: Разность между температурой воздуха и точкой росы называют дефицитом точки росы.
При меньшей точке росы в воздухе меньше влаги.

answers.text: В обоих одинаково: температура воздуха одинакова
answers.note: Относительная влажность зависит и от температуры, и от содержания влаги.

answers.text: Нельзя определить по точке росы; нужен индекс жары
answers.note: Индекс жары описывает ощущаемое тепло с учётом температуры и относительной влажности.

currentCard.explanation: При одинаковой температуре образец с более высокой точкой росы содержит больше водяного пара. Поэтому больше влаги в первом образце.

source.title: NOAA National Weather Service Glossary: Dew Point

groups: NWS states that a higher dew point indicates more moisture. Equal temperature makes the16-versus8 comparison direct; heat index measures perceived heat.

Unique key0 requires applying the moisture relation to two explicitly ordered samples. First/second choices have identical29-character lengths and both repeat dew point; neither receives a unique root or formatting cue. Equal-temperature and heat-index distractors express plausible indicator confusions.
Higher dew point means more moisture in the complete entry.
Connects the general relation to the stated first sample, so the numerical comparison is explained.
Dew Point Depression is explicitly the air-temperature minus dew-point difference.
Adds the useful name and meaning of a different derived quantity, beyond identifying the wetter sample.
The higher-dew-point moisture relation supports the corresponding lower-dew-point comparison here.
Gives a positive moisture fact and directly explains why the8-degree sample cannot be the wetter one.
RH depends on both moisture content and temperature.
Corrects the equal-temperature shortcut by identifying the independent moisture input.
Heat Index combines actual temperature and RH to describe apparent heat.
Explains the alternative indicator positively and distinguishes its purpose from ranking vapor content.
classReview: The source supplies a relationship, not the numerical answer.
The solver must compare16 and8 and apply the relationship under a fixed-temperature condition; this is an application rather than a requested definition.
metadataReview: Captured Dew Point entry supports the central relation.
Title and URL identify the relevant primary definition; date denotes verification of the saved capture.

currentCard.prompt: В образце при текущей температуре содержится 8 г/м³ водяного пара, а насыщению соответствуют 20 г/м³. Какую относительную влажность следует указать?

answers.note: Относительная влажность зависит и от фактического содержания влаги, и от температуры.
До насыщения не хватает 12 г/м³, то есть 60% от заданной ёмкости.
Если в образце было бы 5 г/м³ при ёмкости 20 г/м³, относительная влажность составила бы 25%.
Если бы в образце было 16 г/м³, это было бы 80% от ёмкости 20 г/м³.

currentCard.explanation: Относительная влажность равна отношению фактического содержания пара к количеству при насыщении, выраженному в процентах. Здесь 8 / 20 = 0,4, то есть 40%.

source.title: NOAA National Weather Service Glossary: Relative Humidity

groups: NWS defines RH as actual moisture divided by saturation moisture, in percent.8/20 times100 is40.
All four options use identical percentage formatting and length.60 is the missing fraction,80 can arise from mishandling8, and25 is another plausible fraction error. Only40 applies the stated ratio.
Definition and independently checked arithmetic support8/20=0.4=40%.
Shows both the governing ratio and its application, rather than merely naming the answer.
The complete entry explicitly makes RH a function of moisture and temperature.
Adds the temperature dependence beyond the fixed-temperature calculation.
20-8=12 and12/20=60%; arithmetic uses the sourced ratio.
Explains the precise complement error while making a true statement about the remaining capacity.
5/20=25% follows from the same sourced ratio.
Explicit counterfactual does not misstate the actual sample; it shows the amount that would make this alternative true.
16/20=80% follows from the same sourced ratio.
Explicit counterfactual distinguishes16 from the actual8 and supplies a positive calculation.
classReview: RH is a dimensionless percentage ratio.
Requires selecting the actual/saturation ratio and converting it to a percentage; the label is supported by an actual operation.
metadataReview: Primary RH entry supports definition and temperature dependence.
Citation directly matches the quantity being calculated.

currentCard.prompt: Сравнивают психрометры в очень влажном и очень сухом воздухе. В каком случае разность показаний сухого и смоченного термометров будет меньше?

answers.note: Психрометр — гигрометр с двумя сходными термометрами; смоченная колба охлаждается испарением.
В сухом воздухе психрометрическая разность соответствует большей сухости атмосферы.

answers.text: Разность не зависит от сухости воздуха
answers.note: Психрометр относится к приборам для измерения содержания водяного пара в воздухе.
В sling-психрометре прибор вращают, чтобы обеспечить вентиляцию и испарение со смоченной колбы.

currentCard.explanation: Испарение охлаждает смоченный термометр, а разность его показания с сухим служит мерой сухости. Поэтому меньшая разность указывает на менее сухой, то есть более влажный, воздух.

source.title: NOAA National Weather Service Glossary: Psychrometer

groups: Psychrometer definition links evaporative cooling and the reading difference to atmospheric dryness; the intended comparison yields a smaller difference in moist air.

Requires interpreting an instrument difference rather than naming wet-bulb temperature. Moist/dry alternatives are parallel23/21-character phrases. Independence and zero alternatives express plausible misconceptions; their absolutes do not distinguish between the two close primary choices.
The full entry supports cooling by evaporation and difference as a dryness measure.
Connects the mechanism, measured difference and wetter-air conclusion.
The source identifies two similar thermometers, a wet bulb and evaporation cooling.
Adds instrument construction and mechanism beyond the selected environment.
Difference is a measure of atmospheric dryness.
Positively explains the dry-air alternative rather than merely marking it wrong.
Psychrometer is explicitly an instrument measuring air water-vapor content.
Its actual measuring purpose contradicts the claimed independence from dryness.
Complete Sling Psychrometer entry states that whirling provides ventilation for evaporation.
A concrete operating fact explains active evaporation; it is useful even though it does not exhaustively quantify the zero-difference misconception.
classReview: The entry supplies the instrument mechanism and dryness interpretation.
The solver maps greater dryness to the reading difference, then selects the opposite moist condition for a smaller difference.
metadataReview: Psychrometer and Sling Psychrometer complete entries support these fields.
The source is a factual definition. S13 NoMatches is unnecessary and is not used.

currentCard.prompt: В двух местах измерена одинаковая температура воздуха. В более влажном месте жара ощущается сильнее. Какой показатель описывает это ощущаемое тепло?

answers.note: Точка росы — температура достижения насыщения при охлаждении воздуха без изменения его давления и влагосодержания.
Индекс жары, или кажущаяся температура, сочетает фактическую температуру воздуха с относительной влажностью.
Относительная влажность — процентное отношение атмосферной влаги к количеству при насыщении.
В психрометре смоченный термометр охлаждается испарением, а разность его показания с сухим отражает сухость.

currentCard.explanation: Индекс жары учитывает относительную влажность вместе с фактической температурой воздуха и описывает, насколько жарко ощущается.

source.title: NOAA National Weather Service Glossary: Heat Index

groups: Heat Index is the apparent-heat measure combining actual temperature and RH; the other choices have distinct sourced purposes. Key1 is factually unique.

The stem says «жара», and only «Индекс жары» repeats that answer root. A solver can select it lexically without interpreting the same-temperature humidity comparison. This is the same kind of avoidable answer-family leakage as the earlier Snow cue. Lengths10/11/23/30 do not independently single out the key, and the indicator alternatives are plausible, but the root cue remains blocking.
Complete Heat Index entry supports both inputs and perceived heat.
Explains what the combined indicator represents; the explanation itself is useful and accurate.
Dew Point definition includes saturation by cooling at constant pressure and moisture.
Gives the alternative indicator's actual meaning and conditions.
The source names Apparent Temperature and its temperature/RH combination.
Adds the synonym «кажущаяся температура» and explicit combined inputs beyond the selected label.
RH is the percent moisture/saturation ratio.
A positive definition separates a moisture proportion from perceived heat.
Psychrometer entry supports evaporation cooling and dryness from wet/dry readings.
Explains the physical measurement behind the alternative; no definition is inferred from NoMatches.
classReview: Sources establish the indicator's definition but do not establish difficulty.

CURRENT can be solved by «жара → индекс жары». The two-place scenario does not force an operation beyond selecting the named apparent-heat indicator. Meaningful medium is not demonstrated by this composite.
metadataReview: Primary Heat Index entry directly supports the key and explanation.
Title and URL match the factual quantity; editorial hold does not invalidate the citation.
cards.requiredCorrection: Author should remove the answer-root shortcut and make the frozen medium question require interpreting the temperature/humidity relationship. Do not fix the frozen label mechanically.

currentCard.prompt: Ненасыщенная порция воздуха поднялась на 1 км. Давление вокруг неё уменьшилось, теплообмена с окружением не было. Как изменится температура порции?

answers.note: Изменение температуры при расширении или сжатии может происходить без теплообмена с окружением.

answers.text: Понизится: порция расширится и адиабатически охладится
answers.note: У насыщенной порции скорость охлаждения зависит от температуры и давления, в отличие от почти постоянного сухого градиента.

answers.text: Останется прежней: без теплообмена температура не меняется
answers.note: В адиабатическом процессе тепло не передаётся, но температура порции всё же меняется при расширении или сжатии.
Влажноадиабатический градиент относится к насыщенной порции и меняется в зависимости от её температуры и давления.

currentCard.explanation: При снижении давления ненасыщенная порция расширяется; без поступления тепла она охлаждается. Для такого сухого подъёма градиент близок к 9,8 °C на километр.

source.title: NOAA National Weather Service Glossary: Adiabatic

groups: Adiabatic entry explicitly links ascent and expansion to cooling without heat exchange; unsaturated lapse rate is9.8°C/km. Only key1 has the consistent mechanism.

The solver must distinguish heat transfer from temperature change and infer expansion from lower pressure. Alternatives encode reversed pressure response, constant-temperature confusion and a false condensation prerequisite. Key54 characters is shorter than the58-character constant-temperature distractor; no unique length cue.
Ascent cooling and9.8°C/km for unsaturated parcels are directly sourced.
Supplies the causal chain and a quantitative consequence beyond selecting cooling.
Temperature can change through expansion/compression without exchanged heat.
Positive process fact is useful; it does not endorse the distractor's erroneous assertion that falling external pressure compresses the parcel.
Dry lapse rate is constant; moist rate depends on parcel temperature and pressure.
Adds the saturated-versus-unsaturated rate distinction beyond the question's cooling direction.
Adiabatic changes occur without heat exchange.
Directly corrects the mistaken equation of no heat transfer with no temperature change.
Moist lapse applies to saturated parcels and varies with temperature and pressure.
Explains the actual domain of the condensation-related alternative.
classReview: Requires a causal inference and rejection of no-heat/no-temperature-change confusion; it does not merely ask for a gradient name.
metadataReview: Complete Adiabatic, Adiabatic Lapse Rate and Moist Adiabatic Lapse Rate entries support the fields.
Primary URL includes the relevant complete entries.

currentCard.prompt: Зондирование показывает слой с ростом температуры вверх. Основание слоя совпадает с поверхностью земли, а не расположено выше неё. Какой тип слоя наблюдается?

answers.note: При адиабатическом процессе температура порции меняется при расширении или сжатии без теплообмена с окружением.
Инверсия — рост температуры с высотой; если основание слоя находится выше поверхности, инверсия называется приподнятой.
У приподнятой инверсии основание слоя расположено выше земной поверхности.
Оседание воздуха — широкая область нисходящего движения; оно может сформировать отдельный тип инверсии.

currentCard.explanation: Приземная инверсия начинается у поверхности; приподнятая инверсия имеет основание выше неё. В обоих случаях температура в слое увеличивается с высотой.

source.title: NOAA National Weather Service Glossary: Inversion

groups: Temperature Inversion entry explicitly distinguishes surface-based and elevated bases. Ground-level base uniquely selects key1.

Requires identifying the rising-temperature profile and choosing its spatial subtype. The closest two alternatives are parallel inversion names of32/34 characters; adiabatic cooling and subsidence are processes rather than this profile. Ground location is the substantive classification criterion.
The complete entry states both subtype bases and temperature increase with height.
Explains both the common property and distinguishing criterion.
Adiabatic refers to a parcel's expansion/compression temperature change without heat exchange.
Defines the different process positively instead of treating it as a vertical environmental profile.
Inversion means increasing temperature with height; an above-surface base is elevated.
Adds the opposite subtype's name and criterion beyond the ground-level key.
Elevated inversion has its base above the surface.
Direct positive definition explains why this closely related alternative fails the stated base condition.
Subsidence is broad descent and can produce a subsidence inversion aloft.
Separates a possible formation process from the observed profile's classification.
classReview: Source supplies both profile and subtype conditions.
Two observed properties must be classified: temperature increase and base altitude. Merely recognizing the general word inversion does not choose between the two close inversion options.
metadataReview: Temperature Inversion entry directly supports the subtype distinction.
Citation matches the tested classification; auxiliary process sources are explicitly bound in groups.

currentCard.prompt: Летом нагретая поверхность поднимает приземный воздух. Наблюдаются вертикальные потоки тепла, но облака не формируются. Как называют этот процесс?

answers.note: Адиабатическое охлаждение связано с расширением поднимающейся порции при отсутствии теплообмена.
При инверсии температура растёт с высотой; это характеристика вертикального профиля.
Грозы являются только одной формой конвекции, а не синонимом любого вертикального переноса.
Оседание означает нисходящее движение воздуха над широкой областью.

currentCard.explanation: Конвекция переносит тепло и влагу движением воздуха. Если она происходит без образования облаков, это сухая конвекция. Грозы — лишь одна форма конвекции.

source.title: NOAA National Weather Service Glossary: Convection

groups: Convection entry defines vertical heat transport and explicitly calls convection without cloud formation dry convection. Other choices identify parcel cooling, a temperature profile or descent.

Requires interpreting transport as convection and applying the cloud-absence qualifier. The stem does not say convection or dry. Key15 characters is similar to subsidence16, so shortness is not a unique cue. Adiabatic cooling is a plausible simultaneous parcel effect, but does not name the stated heat-transport process.
Complete Convection entry supports transport, cloudless dry convection and thunderstorms as one form.
Explains the qualifier and broadens the concept beyond thunderstorms.
Ascent expansion causes cooling without heat exchange.
Provides the alternative's real physical process, separate from heat transport by motion.
Temperature inversion is temperature increasing with height.
Positive profile definition distinguishes a vertical distribution from a moving-air process.
NWS expressly says thunderstorms are only one form of convection.
Adds a useful limit on a common synonym, beyond selecting cloudless dry convection.
Subsidence is descent over a broad area.
Gives the alternative's positive direction and scale, contrasting with the observed ascent.
classReview: Source supports the transport category and cloudless subtype.
Must combine motion/heat transport with cloud absence; the answer root is not supplied in the stem.
metadataReview: Full Convection entry includes dry and moist forms.
Citation directly supports the qualifier and keyed additional fact.

currentCard.prompt: Над широкой областью воздух постепенно опускается; при сжатии он нагревается, а выше развивается инверсионный слой. Как называется это нисходящее движение?

answers.note: Адиабатическое охлаждение — изменение температуры поднимающегося воздуха при расширении без теплообмена.
Температурная инверсия — профиль, при котором температура возрастает с высотой.
Инверсия, связанная с оседанием, обычно наблюдается в областях субтропического высокого давления.
Конвекция переносит тепло и влагу вертикальными движениями; грозы — лишь один из её видов.

currentCard.explanation: Оседание — нисходящее движение воздуха на широкой территории. При постепенном опускании воздух сжимается и нагревается; связанная с этим инверсия часто бывает при субтропических областях высокого давления.

source.title: NOAA National Weather Service Glossary: Subsidence

groups: Broad descending motion is Subsidence; its inversion entry explicitly supplies gradual sinking, adiabatic compression warming and an inversion aloft. Key2 is correct.

As a recognition item the question is clear, with plausible neighboring concepts and no unique length/format cue. Convection can include downdrafts, but the broad gradual sinking/warming/inversion pattern identifies subsidence. The class problem is assessed separately: naming descent does not require using all these causal details.
Complete entries support broad descent, compression warming, inversion and subtropical high-pressure association.
Connects the motion, temperature effect and typical pressure setting.
Adiabatic ascent expansion produces cooling without heat exchange.
Positive definition contrasts ascent cooling with the stated descent warming.
Inversion is increasing temperature with height.
Distinguishes the resulting profile from the requested moving-air process.
Subsidence Inversion entry explicitly associates it with subtropical high-pressure areas.
Adds a typical geographic/pressure context absent from the stem and key.
Convection transports heat/moisture vertically; thunderstorms are one form.
Defines the alternative positively without asserting that convection never includes descent.
classReview: The source supports all physical details but does not establish a difficulty level.

CURRENT asks only to name explicitly stated «опускается / нисходящее движение». The warming and inversion clauses can be removed without changing the required solution. It therefore does not require the causal inference expected of frozen medium; the extra details decorate a basic recognition task.
metadataReview: Subsidence and Subsidence Inversion entries directly support all central claims.
Citation matches both the motion and its inversion context.
cards.requiredCorrection: Author should make the frozen medium task depend on the compression/warming/inversion relationship, rather than asking the name of explicitly supplied descent. No difficulty-label edit is authorized by this review.

currentCard.prompt: Как называют крупномасштабную циркуляцию ветров вокруг центра низкого атмосферного давления?

answers.note: Антициклон — крупномасштабная циркуляция вокруг центра высокого давления.
Ложбина — вытянутая область относительно низкого давления, обычно без замкнутой циркуляции.
Гребень — вытянутая область относительно высокого атмосферного давления.
Циклон вращается против часовой стрелки в Северном полушарии и по часовой — в Южном.

currentCard.explanation: Циклон — крупномасштабная циркуляция вокруг центра низкого давления. В Северном полушарии она вращается против часовой стрелки, а в Южном — по часовой.

source.title: NOAA National Weather Service Glossary: Cyclone

groups: Cyclone is large-scale circulation around central low pressure; anticyclone is high, trough elongated low, ridge elongated high.

Four parallel synoptic terms. Low pressure alone makes Trough plausible, while central circulation supplies the distinguishing condition. No cyclone root is given in the stem. Lengths10/7/7/6 are ordinary term lengths rather than a conspicuous keyed sentence.
Definition and both hemispheric directions are directly in the complete entry.
Adds hemispheric rotation beyond the identification criterion.
Anticyclone is circulation around central high pressure.
Positive definition makes the high/low distinction explicit.
Trough is elongated low pressure, usually without closed circulation.
Explains why the low-pressure distractor is not the specified central circulation.
Ridge is an elongated relatively high-pressure area.
Positive description distinguishes pressure sign and geometry.
The source gives counterclockwise north and clockwise south.
Useful hemispheric rotation fact is absent from the question's low-pressure definition.
classReview: Direct primary definition supports the classification.
Basic recognition among related pressure features is meaningful easy.
metadataReview: Complete Cyclone definition supports the key and rotation.
Primary title and URL identify the exact relevant entry.

currentCard.prompt: В Северном полушарии наблюдается крупномасштабное вращение по часовой стрелке вокруг центра. Какой тип центра давления соответствует этой системе?

answers.note: Циклон — крупномасштабная циркуляция вокруг центра низкого давления.
Ложбина — вытянутая область относительно низкого давления, обычно не образующая замкнутую циркуляцию.
Гребень — вытянутая область относительно высокого давления, противоположная ложбине.
Антициклон — крупномасштабная циркуляция вокруг области высокого давления; направление вращения меняется между полушариями.

currentCard.explanation: В Северном полушарии антициклональная циркуляция направлена по часовой стрелке вокруг центра высокого давления; в Южном полушарии направление обратное.

source.title: NOAA National Weather Service Glossary: Anticyclone

groups: In the Northern Hemisphere clockwise central circulation is anticyclonic and high-pressure; cyclone has the opposite direction, and trough/ridge are elongated features.

The choices are parallel named pressure systems. Hemisphere and rotation must be combined to select Anticyclone; pressure sign is not supplied. The somewhat broad phrase «тип центра давления» is intelligible as the named central-pressure system among these choices. Key10 characters is modestly longer than6/7/7 but remains an ordinary single term, with no unique formatting/root cue.
Complete Anticyclone entry supplies central high pressure and both rotation directions.
Explains the inference and explicitly limits it by hemisphere.
Cyclone is circulation around central low pressure.
Positive definition distinguishes the alternative pressure system.
Trough is elongated low pressure, usually not a closed circulation.
Explains geometry and pressure rather than merely rejecting the term.
Ridge is elongated high pressure and opposite to trough.

ownPerTargetComparisons.reason: Umbrella humidity asks a quantity's name; Dew identifies surface liquid deposition; Hygrometer asks an instrument. New Dew Point ranks two samples using different dew points at fixed temperature. RH calculates a fraction; Wet Bulb interprets instrument differences; Heat Index identifies apparent heat. None is the same ranking fact or its simple inverse.

Actual8/saturation20 percentage calculation differs from general humidity naming, instrument purpose, dew-point moisture ranking, psychrometer dryness and perceived heat. The same humidity domain does not make these identical predicates.

Hygrometer names an instrument's measured quantity; inventions Thermometer asks temperature; station Thermometer asks solar shielding. Current Wet Bulb interprets which environment gives a smaller evaporative wet/dry difference. This is not an inverse instrument-purpose question or duplicate humidity calculation.

Apparent heat is distinct from actual-temperature measurement, station exposure protection, moisture ranking, RH calculation and psychrometer dryness. No duplicate found; its separate root-cue/class hold remains.

Dry/moist gradient neighbors ask the applicable gradient name; environmental lapse asks observed surroundings; inversion-positive asks stability. New Adiabatic asks the parcel's temperature response to ascent, pressure decrease and no heat exchange. It is not merely the inverse of naming a dry lapse rate. Inversion classifies a profile, Convection classifies transport, Subsidence names broad descent.

Environmental lapse asks the measured gradient; inversion-positive asks which profile suppresses convection. Current Inversion additionally discriminates surface-based versus elevated base. Parcel lapse, cooling, transport and subsidence are different predicates; none asks the same base-altitude subtype or its inverse.

Convectional Rain requires a summer precipitation/cloud process, while the new target explicitly excludes clouds and identifies dry heat transport. CAPE asks energy availability; cloud species ask cloud identity. Adiabatic cooling, inversion profile and broad descent are related but distinct. The cloudless qualifier makes this more than a reversal of the rain question.

Broad descent with compression warming differs from ascent cooling, gradient naming, stable profile classification, cloudless convection and hemisphere-dependent pressure-system identification. Inversion may result from subsidence, but naming motion is not naming the profile. No duplicate found; the frozen-medium hold is independent.

Generic central-low circulation differs from elongated trough/ridge geometry; Atlantic hurricane naming; tropical stages, naming threshold and category; extratropical fronts; two-cyclone interaction; sting jet; rapid deepening. Anticyclone target tests hemisphere-conditioned rotation-to-system inference rather than the same supplied low-pressure definition.

Clockwise Northern Hemisphere circulation requires identifying an anticyclonic center. Ridge and trough ask elongated geometry. Cyclone target supplies low pressure and asks its name, while this target supplies rotation and hemisphere. Specialized cyclone stages/features do not test this inference. Opposite system names alone do not make the two targets an identical fact or a simple question-answer inversion.
